title: Incorrect file permissions after backup via sftp

Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.24.1 on linux/amd64


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------
sftp 


Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------
Similar to #4447, but affecting backup files.

"restic backup" is creating data files with user (and for my case group) read-write permission when the repo is accessed via sftp:restic@participant4, while the local files (on repohost) are all read only.

For example, the first of these data files was created during a local backup (as root on repohost), and the other during a sftp backup (to sftp:restic@participant4:...), both to the same repo.

```
1887814808    628 -r--r-----   1 root     restic     640063 Sep  5 22:39 ./index/5bebf47942e1d47fd25453f42c3d53dcd43959cc4898e7f27230307b9ea93405
1612200155     28 -rw-rw----   1 restic   restic      26374 Sep  5 22:58 ./index/9587e9696220eda5f2611ca508e6e5b5ac7c27faca544ee84e96f66434abb61c
```

<!--
This section should include at least:

 * A description of the problem you are having with restic.

 * The complete command line and any environment variables you used to
   configure restic's backend access. Make sure to replace sensitive values!

 * The output of the commands, what restic prints gives may give us much
   information to diagnose the problem!

 * The more time you spend describing an easy way to reproduce the behavior (if
   this is possible), the easier it is for the project developers to fix it!
-->


Expected behavior
-----------------
All repo files uploaded by sftp should have the same permission as if the repo file was created by a local backup.

Actual behavior
---------------
Repo files have read-write permission instead of read-only.

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------
Probably something similar to #4447.

Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------
restic makes me happy every day (at 3am).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Are the restic versions used to make the files the same?

This can hardly be the same problem as #4447, because in this instance, restic does an explicit chmod after creating the file. I'm not sure why it adds write permission; this happens in internal/backend/util/paths.go, but the discussion surrounding that code in #3419 doesn't mention it (or I'm glossing over it...).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
## Reproducible test case

Context: 

Both restic server (below, `participant4`) and restic client (`clienthost`) are using restic 0.18.0.

The test case initializes repository /var/restic/test, adjusts it for [Group Accessible Repository](https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/030_preparing_a_new_repo.html#group-accessible-repositories) 
(though its instructions are outdated), then performs a backup on server, then on client.

Parent directory participant4:/var/restic has group restic mode g+s
Repohost is Rocky 9, with its packaged ssh/sftp server.
 
1. After local init, notice that directories inherit g+s but no g+rwx (on its own, not a bug, but it gives me an idea... see below)
```
root@participant4# restic init -r /var/restic/test
restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.24.1 on linux/amd64

root@participant4# restic init -r /var/restic/test

root@participant4# ls -ld . test test/* test/keys/*
drwxrwsr-x.   5 restic restic 60 Sep  6 09:12 .
drwxrws---.   7 root restic   87 Sep  6 09:12 test
-r--------.   1 root restic  155 Sep  6 09:12 test/config
drwx--S---. 258 root restic 8192 Sep  6 09:12 test/data
drwx--S---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/index
drwx--S---.   2 root restic   78 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys
-r--------.   1 root restic  454 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys/120771e73ad01220d32b72923a5ce7426dc6797307eb876d2301c43e0f0df9dc
drwx--S---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/locks
drwx--S---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/snapshots
```
2. Prepare for multi-use (though note that instructions in docs at [Group accessible repositories](https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/030_preparing_a_new_repo.html#group-accessible-repositories):
```
# find test -type d -exec chmod 2770  {} \;
# find test -type f -exec chmod 0440 {} \; 
```
- Here are the resulting permissions, which look good.  The keys file is group readable.
```
# ls -ld test test/* test/keys/*
drwxrws---.   7 root restic   87 Sep  6 09:12 test
-r--r-----.   1 root restic  155 Sep  6 09:12 test/config
drwxrws---. 258 root restic 8192 Sep  6 09:12 test/data
drwxrws---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/index
drwxrws---.   2 root restic   78 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys
-r--r-----.   1 root restic  454 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys/120771e73ad01220d32b72923a5ce7426dc6797307eb876d2301c43e0f0df9dc
drwxrws---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/locks
drwxrws---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:12 test/snapshots
```
3. Run a local backup on a single file.  Results are good.  Newly created index file is group readable.
```
root@participant4# restic backup -r /var/restic/test /etc/services
...

root@participant4# ls -ld test test/* test/keys/* test/index/*
drwxrws---.   7 root restic   87 Sep  6 09:12 test
-r--r-----.   1 root restic  155 Sep  6 09:12 test/config
drwxrws---. 258 root restic 8192 Sep  6 09:12 test/data
drwxrws---.   2 root restic   78 Sep  6 09:41 test/index
-r--r-----.   1 root restic  364 Sep  6 09:41 test/index/1121d5b03ec5bd3e9dce12d6a5dd94161ec36b2cb1babf29bf59b71a4755cfa4
drwxrws---.   2 root restic   78 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys
-r--r-----.   1 root restic  454 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys/120771e73ad01220d32b72923a5ce7426dc6797307eb876d2301c43e0f0df9dc
drwxrws---.   2 root restic    6 Sep  6 09:41 test/locks
drwxrws---.   2 root restic   78 Sep  6 09:41 test/snapshots
```
4. Backup on client, check file perms on server.  Note the new index file created via sftp has incorrect g+rw permission. (I didn't show the data directory files, but they also show incorrect g+rw permission)
```
root@participant5# restic version
restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.24.1 on linux/amd64

root@participant5# restic -r sftp:<email-scrubbed>:/var/restic/test backup /etc/services
...

root@participant6# # ls -ld test test/* test/keys/* test/index/*
drwxrws---.   7 root   restic   87 Sep  6 09:12 test
-r--r-----.   1 root   restic  155 Sep  6 09:12 test/config
drwxrws---. 258 root   restic 8192 Sep  6 09:12 test/data
drwxrws---.   2 root   restic  150 Sep  6 09:43 test/index
-r--r-----.   1 root   restic  364 Sep  6 09:41 test/index/1121d5b03ec5bd3e9dce12d6a5dd94161ec36b2cb1babf29bf59b71a4755cfa4
-rw-rw----.   1 restic restic  272 Sep  6 09:43 test/index/1abe9de6544aa91aa10a266aab46405ade4d8b846a2d67cedbe555260a0112f7
drwxrws---.   2 root   restic   78 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys
-r--r-----.   1 root   restic  454 Sep  6 09:12 test/keys/120771e73ad01220d32b72923a5ce7426dc6797307eb876d2301c43e0f0df9dc
drwxrws---.   2 root   restic    6 Sep  6 09:43 test/locks
drwxrws---.   2 root   restic  150 Sep  6 09:43 test/snapshots
```

## Expected:

- That restic on the clienthost should have created files on the server with mode 0440.
- That instructions in doc should present absolute (e.g. 2770 or u=rwx,g=rwxs,o=) modes to adjust the repo for group accessibilty, rather than relative modifications (since restic is fully opinionated as to what those modes should be).
- That the doc remove the the doc section on Group repository "read-write access", since restic does not require file write access to operate, and modifying a file outside restic likely corrupts the repo.  It read to me like if I want to perform a backup, I have to enable read-write access on files.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> That restic on the participant5 should have created files on the server with mode 0440.

This is an omission in the sftp backend. Anyone up for a PR to add the missing chmod call?

> That instructions in doc should present absolute (e.g. 2770 or u=rwx,g=rwxs,o=) modes to adjust the repo for group accessibilty, rather than relative modifications (since restic is fully opinionated as to what those modes should be).

Included in https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5489 .

> That the doc remove the the doc section on Group repository "read-write access", since restic does not require file write access to operate, and modifying a file outside restic likely corrupts the repo

Without write access to the repository directories, one won't be able to modify the repository. So it makes sense to differentiate between both cases. The unintended file write permissions in the docs are fixed by https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5489 .

comments.body:
> Without write access to the repository directories, one won't be able to modify the repository. So it makes sense to differentiate between both cases. The unintended file write permissions in the docs are fixed by https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5489 .

Yes indeed.  Thank you.

comments.author: participant3
participant1
comments.body:
> This is an omission in the sftp backend. Anyone up for a PR to add the missing chmod call?

The call is there, but the mode comes from DeriveModesFromFileInfo, which sets the write flag.

I think the difference between local and sftp files is caused only by the umask difference. pkg/sftp does not subtract the client umask, so the sftpd process's umask is applied instead.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I think the difference between local and sftp files is caused only by the umask difference.

FWIW the server umask is probably a red herring. I checked the umask of the running (out of the box) sftp-server process, and it is 0022, which would normally remove group write on newly created files, but the failure case shows group write set.  

(Normally umask is only applied file creation time, not via chmod(), so I assume  (assuming f.Chmod eventually causes the sftp-server to do a real chmod()).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The missing bit is not related to DeriveModesFromFileInfo, which returns a writable mode, so the temp file can be written. It is after the final rename of the temp file into place in Save(). On the backend/local, but not on backend/sftp, the final file (writable up until now) is made read-only at the very last step:

local end of Save() function:
https://github.com/restic/restic/blob/c55df65bb6e543f3ff6939c989478a2b28b2a1c5/internal/backend/local/local.go#L192-L200

sftp end of Save() function:
https://github.com/restic/restic/blob/c55df65bb6e543f3ff6939c989478a2b28b2a1c5/internal/backend/sftp/sftp.go#L354-L365

(I'm sorry I don't have any go experience or go toolchain setup, or I'd write/test/push the change straight away)

And get the original mode of the file without group write permissions.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> let me see if I understand correctly, that means that we need to set the file to read-only after renaming the file, correct?
> also then, we use the Chmod after creating the file in order to write into the file.

We could actually mark the file as readonly before renaming it. That way the file permissions are already correct before renaming.

So the order of event would be `create temp file`, `set initial permissions`, `write file content`, `set readonly` and `rename to final name`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: You're right, this isn't the umask. Still, I think we could remove the group permissions earlier, in DeriveModesFromFileInfo. I don't see why we'd set g+w there.
